sources.note: Cited paths only; the identity file records every retrieved file, its digests and its inspection scope, including files read but not cited. performance-ceiling-analysis keeps its own earlier pin for the checkpoint anchor.

applicability.scope: Model-level prefill and decode speed-of-light analysis for decoder-only (optionally multimodal) inference under a declared parallel layout; extends performance-ceiling-analysis L1 from one operation to a whole model without replacing its evidence rules
applicability.hardware: any; per-dtype peaks, memory bandwidth and link bandwidths must be supplied with sources
applicability.prerequisites: Model config and forward source at a pinned revision, the checkpoint's tensor headers where a checkpoint exists, the serving framework release that will run, and the layout and workload; reading the skill does not authorize execution
applicability.input_contract: Model config, forward source and checkpoint headers; serving framework and release with source anchors for every fusion; per-world parallel degrees, ranks per node and node count; batch, input, output, prefix and verify tokens, and the measured expert load skew for MoE; per-dtype compute peaks at the sustained clock, memory and link bandwidths with sources; any launch floor or link latency labelled as an assumption
applicability.produced_artifact: A per-phase table with per-op counts and binding resource, per-resource totals, the conditional bound and its binding resources, the serial per-op estimate, headline TTFT, TPOT and throughput figures each labelled bound or estimate, every anchor and gate result, assumptions and unknowns; analytical only, not a measured result
failure_modes: The serial per-op sum is reported as a bound, or used to reject a faster measurement
Counts come from the unfused graph, overstating launches and activation round-trips, or from fusions the framework does not run, understating bytes
A degree that does not divide a weight is silently replaced by a divisor that does
Expert load skew is left at its default, making routed time and exchange optimistic
A windowed layer is priced as global, or a dense layer as windowed, because the cache growth law was not checked
Prefill attention is counted as a full square rather than causal pairs
An unmeasured launch floor or link latency, or a spec-sheet peak below the sustained clock, enters the bound
A measured envelope replaces the analytical figure instead of sitting beside it
applicability.refusal_point: Stops when an anchor gate fails or cannot be judged, when a per-dtype peak, a link bandwidth or the MoE load skew is missing, or when weights plus one request's KV do not fit a rank; prices an unanchored fusion as unfused and states the error direction; makes no measured, achievable or end-to-end claim

recommendations: Anchor weights, shapes and KV growth before pricing any count, and treat an unjudged gate as a failure.
Price the post-fusion graph the serving framework runs at its pinned release, with a source anchor for every fusion.
Report the resource-total bound and the serial per-op estimate in separate columns; only the bound may reject a result.
Keep unmeasured launch floors and link latencies out of the bound, as labelled assumptions in the estimate.
Keep measured kernel times beside the analytical figure, joined by physical identity rather than model or framework name.

verification.note: Derived from a reviewed external implementation at a pinned commit (references/huggingarch-model-sol.md, identity in references/huggingarch-source-identity.json); claims read from executable code and claims stated only in the project's prose, docstrings included, are marked separately there. The bundled pure helper composes supplied counts only and is covered by synthetic tests; no accelerator, model or source-project run was used, and no predicted figure has been compared with a measurement.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
The serial estimate assumes no overlap between kernels and no pipeline bubble; one link latency is used for every fabric.
Counts are only as good as the anchors and the framework binding behind them; behaviour that lives only in weights or custom runtime code is out of reach.
Decoder-only models, optionally multimodal; encoder-decoder models are out of scope.
